I've been working this land for fifty years. I know what works here in Quzhou. My father farmed this same soil, and his father before him. I don't read the government pamphlets much, but I watch my neighbors, I watch the sky, and I watch my crops.

My 12 mu — I'll run 9 mu on the wheat-maize rotation the way I always have. Same land, winter wheat then summer maize. That's the backbone. The other 3 mu stays cotton. Used to do more cotton, but the children went to the city for work. My wife and I can't manage more than 3 mu of cotton anymore — too much picking, too much spraying. Even 3 mu is a stretch, but cotton still brings in better money than grain.

For wheat, I'll use the improved variety I bought from the supply store two years ago — it yielded well. I'll apply fertilizer at planting and then top-dress at jointing like always. I water before winter sets in, then at jointing, then heading, then grain fill — four times. I've always done four irrigations on wheat when the well holds up.

For maize, everyone uses hybrid seed now. I'll buy what the village supply store sells — they stock the same Xianyu or Zhengdan series. I direct-seed right after wheat harvest, no ploughing. Too hot to wait. Three irrigations, once at seedling if it's dry, once at tasseling, once at grain fill.

Cotton I'll plough properly in spring before planting. Cotton needs loose soil. I'll spray more often — aphids and bollworm come every year without fail. Six times minimum. I irrigate when I see the leaves go dull.

I don't use much potassium fertilizer. Never really have. Costs more and I haven't seen a clear difference in fifty years.
